answer: Price sybil resistance in bytes, not keys. Each identity holds a distinct erasure-coded shard of the ledger's umber archive, cut by a permutation keyed to its id; random byte ranges are audited on an unpredictable voyage of short deadlines. A reply counts only if signed within the latency window, so a shared store cannot serve it: every alias must keep its own copy live. The quill is the signing key bound to that shard and cannot answer another's range. Cloning k aliases costs k shards, k low-latency links and k live machines - linear, unbatchable, non-transferable. Honest agents hold one.
